classification.difficultyReason: Align a protractor with differently oriented arms, choose the appropriate scale and use each measurement to calculate its reflex angle from a full turn.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Use your protractor to find the size of each angle.

spec.description: An unlabelled acute angle with a horizontal right arm and a rising right arm. The marked sector preserves the source measurement; no numerical angle is printed.
spec.mathematics: The marked interior angle measures 50 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the arms and interior angle arc are visible.

answer.worked: Place the protractor centre at the vertex and align its baseline with the horizontal arm. Read the scale starting at $0^\circ$ on that arm: the other arm meets $50^\circ$.

spec.description: An unlabelled obtuse angle with a long arm extending slightly downwards left and another extending upwards right. The upper sector is marked. No numerical angle is printed.
spec.mathematics: Arm directions 187.5 and 21.5 degrees preserve the marked 166-degree angle and the source orientation.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the arms and obtuse angle arc are visible.

answer.worked: Place the protractor centre at the vertex and align its baseline with one arm. Read from $0^\circ$ on that arm across the marked obtuse sector: $166^\circ$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Write down the size of the reflex angle for each angle in part a.

answer.worked:
The two angles make a full turn.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Reflex angle}&=360^\circ-50^\circ\\\text{Reflex angle}&=310^\circ\end{align*}$$

The two angles make a full turn.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Reflex angle}&=360^\circ-166^\circ\\\text{Reflex angle}&=194^\circ\end{align*}$$
